title: Using Raw Primitives for Domain Identifiers
pattern: Using the same generic integer or UUID primitive (`u64`, `Uuid`) for distinct domain entity identifiers.
why_bad: It strips identifier context. Callers can easily pass a `class_id` as the `student_id` parameter, compiling perfectly but causing silent data corruption and runtime logical errors.
detection: Function signatures taking multiple parameters of the exact same primitive numeric/UUID type whose names imply distinct domain IDs.
counterexample:
General math coordinates or indices where values are raw bounds:
```rust
fn get_matrix_element(row: usize, col: usize) { ... }
```
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (Chapter 10, p. 325); *Domain Modeling made Functional* (p. 83).
